title: Replace the whole relay role matrix through relay-roles apply
lead: *Proposed.* `slicer relay-roles apply` also accepts `{"expect"?, "replace": {"rows": [...], "rules": [...]}}`: a complete matrix that replaces the current one. slicer turns it into the same steps an `ops` set has (add, set, remove, move, rule-add, rule-edit, rule-remove), so validation, `expect`, `--dry-run`, atomicity, history and the result shape are those of `relay-roles-apply`. A tool can copy a matrix from one project to another, or keep a matrix as a file, and apply it in one step.
findings_note: ork owner answer 2026-11-02 (interactive): the apply form also takes a complete matrix to replace the current one
boundary: **Not in this slice:** changing the file schema, resetting the id counters, keeping ids from another project's matrix, the merge driver, `recommend`, any ork code.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner, 2026-11-02 (interactive, in an ork session): the apply form must also take a whole matrix, with the same validation, revision check, dry run and atomicity. An `ops` list says how to change a matrix the tool has read; a replace says what the matrix should be, which is what a tool that holds a desired matrix (for example one copied from another project, whose row ids differ) has. The first item gives the step engine; this item adds the form that derives the steps.

Interface (*proposed*):
- `replace.rows` is the full ordered list of rows; each row is an object with the keys `show --json` prints (`role`, `when` or the flat condition keys of an `add` step, `agent`, `vendor`, `model`, `reasoning`, `note`), and an optional `id`. `replace.rules` is the full ordered list of `{id?, text}`. A top-level object has `ops` or `replace`, never both (`usage`).
- A row or rule with an `id` that is in the current matrix keeps that id; its fields become exactly the ones given (a missing text field is `""`, a missing condition is any). A row or rule without an `id` is added with the next id; the counters never move backwards. An `id` that is not in the current matrix is refused (`unknown_role_row`, `unknown_role_rule`), so a replace can never reuse or invent an id. A current row or rule whose id is absent from `replace` is removed.
- The derived steps run in this order: removes, sets, adds, then moves so the rows end in the given order, then rule removes, rule edits, rule adds. A rule's order is the order given; rules have no move verb today, so a replace whose rule order differs from the result of those steps is refused with `usage` naming the rule (see the manifest of the ork drafter; an implementer may instead add rule ordering if the slicer owner agrees).
- `steps` in the result lists the derived steps with `changed`. A replace equal to the current matrix derives no changed step, writes nothing and exits 0.
- `rows: []` is allowed and removes every row; a replace with no `rows` key is `usage`.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/roles.py` (the replace parser and the diff to steps, pure).
- `src/slicer/ops.py` (`roles_apply` accepts a replace and runs the derived steps through the same path).
- `src/slicer/cli.py` (`cmd_relay_roles_apply`: the text form says `replace: N steps`).
- `tests/test_relay_roles.py`
- `docs/commands.md` (the Relay roles section at `:751`) and `docs/agents.md` (the `apply` row).
- `CHANGELOG.md`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_RelayRolesApply_ReplaceWithShowOutput_IsNoChange`: the `rows` and `rules` of `show --json` passed as `replace` give `changed: false`, no write, no history.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_Replace_KeepsIdsAddsNewRemovesAbsent`: a replace that keeps r1 with a new model, drops r2, and adds a row without id: r1 keeps its id and gets the model, r2 is gone, the new row gets the next id, history has one `set`, one `remove`, one `add`.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_Replace_OrdersRowsAsGiven`: a replace that lists r3 before r1 ends in that order, through `move` steps.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_Replace_UnknownId_IsRefused`: a row with id `r99` is `unknown_role_row` and nothing is written.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_Replace_SameValidation`: a bad role, an effort of 4 or a newline in a note is refused with the same code as the single verbs, and the problem names `replace.rows[N]`.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_Replace_StaleExpect_IsRefused`: as for `ops`.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_Replace_DryRun_ListsTheDerivedSteps`: `--dry-run --json` lists the steps and the result matrix, and writes nothing.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_ReplaceAndOps_IsUsage`: both keys, or `replace` without `rows`.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_Replace_FromAnotherProject`: the rows of project A without their ids, replaced into project B, give B's matrix the same rows in the same order with B's own new ids.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Start after `relay-roles-apply` has landed, in a new worktree, as that item says.
2. Write the failing tests; see each fail.
3. A pure function from (current matrix, replace) to a list of steps; run them with `roles_apply`'s step path. No second write path.
4. Docs; CHANGELOG.
5. Do not change the file schema or the counters' meaning.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full discover in the background.
- `slicer check`, `git diff --check` in the worktree.
- In a scratch project: `show --json` into a file, edit one model, apply it as `replace` with `--dry-run`, then for real.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the feature branch: "relay-roles apply: replace the whole matrix". Merging waits for the owner.
